name: Air Fryer Apple Pie Bombs
desc: Split biscuit dough wrapped around apple pie filling, air fried, then dipped in butter and spiced sugar.

source.title: Apple Pie Bombs in the Air Fryer
source.evidence: Same six ingredients in the same amounts (3/4 cup sugar, 1 tbsp apple pie spice, 8-count Grands not Flaky Layers, 1 cup chopped filling, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 cup melted butter); this one air fries at 350°F instead of 330°F.

ingredients.raw: 1 (16.3 oz, 8-count) can Pillsbury Grands biscuits (the original, not Flaky Layers)
ingredients.note: 16.3 oz, 8-count; the original, not Flaky Layers

ingredients.raw: 1 cup (243 g) canned apple pie filling, apples chopped into 1/2-inch pieces
Nonstick cooking spray, for the basket

steps: Stir the sugar and apple pie spice together in a shallow bowl and set aside.
Chop the apples in the pie filling into 1/2-inch pieces, then stir the cinnamon into 1 cup of the filling.
Separate each biscuit into 2 thinner layers (16 pieces). Roll or press each into a 4-inch circle.
Spoon about 1 tbsp filling into the center of each circle. Pull the edges up over the filling, pinch the seams tightly closed with no gaps, and roll into a ball.
Preheat the air fryer to 350°F. Lightly spray the basket and arrange the balls seam side down, about 1 inch apart. Work in batches.
Air fry 8-9 minutes, until puffed and golden brown all over.
While each batch is still hot, dip the bombs in the melted butter, then roll them in the spiced sugar. Serve warm.
tips: Fabulessly Frugal's version air fries at 330°F for 8 minutes, flips, then cooks 2 to 4 minutes more; this one runs hotter and skips the flip.
A tight seal matters more than anything else: a gap or thin spot lets the filling leak and burn in the basket.
